players.name: Kenneth Walker III
players.note: Workload and current draft-market support remain strong; allow a slightly earlier selection without changing his core projection.

players.name: Jayden Reed
players.note: Recent ADP movement is positive; preserve upside treatment while market catches up.

players.name: Cam Skattebo
players.note: Recovery and depth-chart movement improve the probability of a meaningful early-season role.

players.name: Dalton Kincaid
players.note: Mid-tier tight ends have been falling in consensus; keep him as value only when the room price discounts the uncertainty.

players.name: Mike Evans
players.note: Evans returned to practice on Sep. 2 after the adductor/groin absence and is now trending toward Week 1 availability. Keep only a small soft-tissue and chemistry discount because he missed much of camp and still needs to avoid a setback during game-week practices.

players.name: Stefon Diggs
players.note: Washington's projected high-snap role plus a sharp ECR rise support a modest upgrade; keep the bump restrained until regular-season target share is confirmed.

players.name: Alvin Kamara
players.note: Grade 2 MCL sprain carries a reported 4-6 week recovery window, creating a real risk of missed early-season games; apply a material but not season-long discount.

players.name: Jordyn Tyson
players.note: Hamstring injury is expected to sideline him roughly two months, pushing his likely return toward October; downgrade early-season availability and rookie-role certainty.

players.name: Chuba Hubbard
players.note: Hubbard returned to practice this week after the hamstring strain and is trending toward normal Week 1 availability, so most of the injury discount can come off. Keep a small role/efficiency caution because Carolina still plans a committee and his 2025 missed-tackle, explosive-run and yards-after-contact profile lagged badly.

players.name: Jonathon Brooks
players.note: Brooks still has real upside and Dave Canales is optimistic he will be ready for Week 1, but he worked off to the side with general soreness on consecutive practices just as Hubbard returned. Trim the earlier upgrade rather than erase it: the committee path remains intact, but immediate workload certainty is lower.

players.name: Malik Nabers
players.note: Nabers progressed again on Sep. 2 by handling both individual and team drills after taking most team reps the day before. That improves the Week 1 outlook, but keep the bump modest because the Giants still have not guaranteed a full opener workload after his ACL/meniscus rehab.

players.name: Breece Hall
players.note: Hall is already doing agility work and was reported moving well while recovering from the groin strain, keeping him on schedule for Week 1; retain only a minimal early-ramp discount.

players.name: Parker Washington
players.note: ECR has climbed sharply on a projected every-down/top-target role and a strong late-2025 finish, but an undisclosed day-to-day injury tempers the upgrade; keep only a modest value bump.

players.name: De'Zhaun Stribling
players.note: Eleven catches for 109 yards across two preseason games, including four catches on five targets over 14 snaps in Week 2, support an immediate role; a day-to-day shoulder injury keeps the bump conservative.

players.name: Makai Lemon
players.note: Lemon is now fully healthy and drew five targets in 17 offensive snaps in his preseason debut, with Nick Sirianni saying the Eagles expect to count on him this year. The drop that became an interception and a muffed punt keep the adjustment neutral-to-slightly cautious rather than a full upgrade.

players.name: Alec Pierce
players.note: Pierce practiced again on Sep. 1 after being activated from PUP, strengthening the Week 1 availability case. Retain only a small ramp-up discount because he missed most of camp after ankle surgery and Keenan Allen still adds target competition.

players.name: Antonio Williams
players.note: Stefon Diggs' arrival materially narrows Williams' path to two-wide and full-time three-wide snaps, matching a recent ECR decline; treat him as a deeper rotational upside play.

players.name: Deebo Samuel Sr.
players.note: A return to San Francisco plus a likely hybrid receiving/rushing role has moved him well up ECR; modestly improve late-round value while acknowledging a crowded and injured receiver room.

players.name: Woody Marks
players.note: He produced 43 yards on five touches with the first-team offense in Preseason Week 2, including a 20-yard touchdown; the split with David Montgomery remains unresolved, so reward efficiency without assuming a takeover.

players.name: Ashton Jeanty
players.note: Jeanty still did not practice on Sep. 2, but Klint Kubiak explicitly said he is optimistic Jeanty will play Week 1 and that the ankle continues to improve. Soften the prior availability penalty slightly while retaining meaningful early workload/ramp risk, especially with Mike Washington Jr. positioned for a real complementary role.

players.name: Mike Washington Jr.
players.note: Washington ran 8 times for 49 yards with the first team in the finale after earlier preseason bursts of 53 and 33 yards. Kubiak now says both Washington and Jeanty are preparing to play a lot, giving Washington some standalone role value in addition to elite handcuff upside.

players.name: Tyrone Tracy Jr.
players.note: He worked behind Devin Singletary with the starters, lost a red-zone fumble, and now sits in a crowded room with Cam Skattebo and Najee Harris; roster and role uncertainty justify a meaningful late-round discount.

players.name: Jadarian Price
players.note: Price still projects as Seattle's lead early-down runner with Charbonnet on PUP, but fresh role reporting has George Holani handling much of the third-down, short-yardage and goal-line work. Keep a modest upgrade for carry volume and draft capital, while trimming the earlier bump because the highest-value touches are likely to be split.

players.name: George Holani
players.note: Seattle's current plan gives Holani a meaningful passing-down, pass-protection, short-yardage and goal-line role while Jadarian Price handles most early downs. Add a small late-round value bump, but keep it conservative because Charbonnet can reclaim work after PUP and Price remains the lead rusher.

players.name: George Kittle
players.note: Kittle is traveling with San Francisco to Australia after encouraging recent practices and is now expected to play Week 1. Increase availability confidence modestly, but preserve normal post-Achilles caution because his snap load and explosiveness in the opener are still unproven.

players.name: MarShawn Lloyd
players.note: Josh Jacobs is now on the Commissioner's Exempt List and cannot practice or play, making Lloyd the clear current lead option in Green Bay. FantasyPros' post-news ADP moved Lloyd into roughly RB36/top-100 territory; upgrade materially but stop short of workhorse assumptions because Chris Brooks will play passing-down snaps and Kaleb Johnson was acquired as insurance.

players.name: Josh Jacobs
players.note: The NFL placed Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List on Aug. 30, making him ineligible to practice or play with no defined return timeline. Green Bay's GM still expects Jacobs to play for the team in 2026, but that does not resolve the current availability block, so retain the heavy draft-value discount without assuming a season-long absence.

players.name: Kaleb Johnson
players.note: Green Bay acquired Johnson after Jacobs was placed on the exempt list. Lloyd remains clearly ahead entering Week 1, but Johnson now has a realistic backup/contingency path in a backfield that suddenly has meaningful available touches; keep the bump small while he learns the offense.

players.name: James Conner
players.note: Arizona placed Conner on injured reserve with a designation to return, guaranteeing at least four missed games while he continues rehabbing the foot/ankle injury that ended his 2025 season. Apply a substantial early-season availability discount without treating the absence as season-ending.

players.name: Jeremiyah Love
players.note: Love is now described as about 50/50 for Week 1 while returning from a high-ankle sprain. He has a good chance to return by Week 2 or 3 if he misses the opener, so apply a moderate early-season health/effectiveness discount rather than lowering his long-term talent projection.

players.name: Tyler Allgeier
players.note: Conner is guaranteed to miss at least four games and Love is only about 50/50 for Week 1, raising Allgeier's early workload floor. Keep the upgrade modest because Love could return quickly and remains the higher-upside long-term lead option.

players.name: Courtland Sutton
players.note: Sutton remains a starter and has played well, but Jaylen Waddle's arrival and Pat Bryant's rise make Denver's target tree more crowded; trim volume expectations slightly rather than downgrading his talent.

players.name: Tony Pollard
players.note: Pollard started Sunday, but Tyjae Spears has logged more starter snaps in each of Tennessee's first two preseason games; treat the backfield as a real committee and shave projected volume modestly.

players.name: Tyjae Spears
players.note: Spears has taken more snaps with Tennessee's starters than Pollard in both preseason games, increasing his committee-role floor; avoid a larger bump because Pollard still started and the offense has struggled.

players.name: Emeka Egbuka
players.note: Todd Bowles' Sep. 1 update moved Egbuka from merely 'hopeful' to still up in the air for Week 1, and he has not yet re-established full team-drill participation after the toe sprain. Increase the early availability/ramp-up discount modestly, but do not alter the underlying WR2/WR1-upside talent case.

players.name: Kayshon Boutte
players.note: Houston should give Boutte more routes than New England would have, but his ADP jumped 37 spots in the final draft week and the fit is less ideal than the market move suggests: his 17.1-yard aDOT matched Drake Maye's elite deep-ball profile, while C.J. Stroud ranked much lower in deep accuracy/completions. Keep only a small role bump and avoid paying through the new price.

players.name: Romeo Doubs
players.note: The Boutte trade further clarifies Doubs as New England's primary outside WR2 behind A.J. Brown in a pass-heavier environment than Green Bay. Reward the cleaner route-volume path modestly while keeping him below true alpha treatment.

players.name: TreVeyon Henderson
players.note: Henderson remained out of practice on Sep. 3 and has not practiced since Aug. 24, making his Week 1 availability materially less certain than the earlier 'good to go' report. When Stevenson was active in 2025, Henderson averaged 11.2 touches and 57.2 total yards and trailed Stevenson in several per-touch and pass-protection metrics. Increase the early availability/committee discount, but preserve long-term explosive upside rather than treating this as a season-long fade.

players.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
players.note: Stevenson remains the favored lead back and his 2025 efficiency/pass-protection edge over Henderson is now reinforced by Henderson missing every practice since Aug. 24. Increase the early-season workload-floor bump slightly, but keep it modest because Henderson could still return soon and retain a meaningful committee role once healthy.

players.name: Tucker Kraft
players.note: Kraft has progressed from ACL rehab into 11-on-11 work and is now expected to be a full participant for Week 1. Restore a modest portion of the injury discount while retaining normal post-ACL early-season caution.

players.name: Chris Bell
players.note: Miami made Bell a clear preseason-finale priority, targeting him five times on the first three possessions, and NFL reporting described him as a player the Dolphins expect to feature in the passing game. Reward the role signal modestly while keeping rookie/quarterback uncertainty intact.

players.name: Chris Olave
players.note: Jordyn Tyson's hamstring absence into roughly October leaves Olave as New Orleans' unquestioned early-season passing-game focal point. His 2025 WR7 points-per-game finish and top-ten target-share/yardage profile support a modest volume-confidence upgrade without chasing the ADP rise.

players.name: Zavion Thomas
players.note: Thomas produced 140 receiving yards and a 97-yard touchdown on five catches in the preseason finale and added a 39-yard punt return, confirming elite field-stretching speed. Keep the bump small because the performance came largely against reserve competition and his regular-season offensive role remains uncertain.

players.name: Isiah Pacheco
players.note: Detroit placed Pacheco on injured reserve with a back injury on Sep. 1, guaranteeing at least four missed games after an already injury-disrupted summer. He was only the projected backup to Jahmyr Gibbs, so the early absence makes him a deep-league stash rather than a normal draft target until the return timeline and role are clearer.

players.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
players.note: Pacheco's four-game minimum IR absence removes Detroit's most experienced backup behind Gibbs and slightly strengthens Gibbs' early-season workload and high-value-touch security. Keep the bump small because Gibbs was already an elite top-of-board option and Detroit still has Jacob Saylors and Sione Vaki available to spell him.
